checks: For every pair the equal-weight coupling of original uniform laws has midpoint density ≤1/v_j and is supported in the actual anchor fiber. Scaling by the smaller area gives two dominated marginals, with respective factors 1 and a_j/b_j.

In a closed cap the midpoint indicator is at most the sum of the endpoint indicators. The midpoint density controls missed, rather than captured, mass on the half-volume complement of a nonvertical through-center trace. Subtracting the missed upper bound from a_j and taking a positive part gives the stated lower credit.

Every reflected endpoint has a unique partner at this anchor, so no mass is counted twice. A pure-base through-cap contains the entire own fiber and at least one of each pair. Parallel tightening handles all containing caps. For one equal-volume pair v_j=v, its formula gives exactly max(k/2,v) as a lower bound, and max(k/2,v)≥(k+2v)/4.

dependencies.hypotheses: Equation (1) applies to two positive-volume actual endpoint fibers, with coefficients 1/2 and integer barycenter p. Its uniform marginals and density bound scale by a_j and compatibility puts the entire midpoint law in K_p.

overlap.comparison: Supplies the joint law and source-capacity accounting for a general barycentric component. The new bound uses symmetry at this particular mark to convert the density ceiling into an explicit missed-mass payment for each pair.
Uses the same one-pair expression in its proof, in a three-fiber problem with a specified alternative endpoint certificate. It does not assemble arbitrary disjoint pairs at the same anchor.
Uses actual reflection intersection of the endpoint bodies. The present certificate needs no reflected containment and uses only the transported volume ceiling.

readability: The displayed notation fixes the cap and mass conventions throughout.
